tweets.text:
this is a very good and well designed report

however, two impt assumptions in it that significantly change the analysis once you start to play with it:

1. the report assumes that jobs can be decomposed into tasks
2. the report models human tasks created by automation always as a fraction of automated tasks. in other words, the underlying assumptions is automation always reduces human labor (or at best leaves it the same)

taken in reverse order:

does automation always reduce human work?
in my experience, the answer is no. automation often creates multiples more work for humans. 

i have a full argument here (https://t.co/Lb7SUCe2pO) for why this is structurally true. but i think any honest analysis of the economic impacts of AI has to take work creation seriously. 

can jobs be decomposed into tasks?
yes, that is a useful lens. but lists of tasks is a way of looking at jobs—one that makes the question of how much of a job is automatable actually tractable. therefore, it's useful.

but this is not the full picture, it's just jobs as exposed to our method of questioning. 

a good example: under this model, where do the new tasks come from? are they just from bosses that add a list to the task list for workers to complete? where do those tasks come from? unless you can model that well you are missing a key term in the analysis (see the first point above.)

another way of looking at this, borrowing from wittgenstein and heidegger, is that a job is a particular way of seeing and caring about the world. an editor notices things a nurse doesn’t, and vice versa. what you care about shapes what you notice, what seems worth doing, and what counts as doing it well. you can make some of that explicit as a task list. but as your tools and circumstances change, the same cares can generate entirely new tasks. that process is part of the job.

the above is completely missing from this analysis (understandably because it's, by definition, very hard to model!) 

but if you take it seriously, it shoudl substantially change your perspective automation and jobs
tweets.summary_zh:
这个报告设计得很好，但有两个重要假设会影响分析结果。首先，报告认为工作可以拆分成任务；其次，报告假设自动化总是减少人类工作。不过，根据我的经验，自动化其实常常会让人类的工作量增加。

我们不能忽视自动化对工作的影响，特别是创造新工作的可能性。虽然将工作分解成任务这个方法有用，但它并不能完整反映工作的全貌。比如，没有考虑新任务的来源，这样的分析就不够全面。工作不仅仅是任务堆叠，而是人们对世界的理解和关心方式。随着工具和环境的变化，新的任务会不断产生。

因此，认真考虑这一点会让我们对自动化和工作的看法大大改变。

tweets.text:
this is a very good and well designed report

however, two impt assumptions in it that significantly change the analysis once you start to play with it:

1. the report assumes that jobs can be decomposed into tasks
2. the report models human tasks created by automation always as a fraction of automated tasks. in other words, the underlying assumptions is automation always reduces human labor (or at best leaves it the same)

taken in reverse order:

does automation always reduce human work?
in my experience, the answer is no. automation often creates multiples more work for humans. 

i have a full argument here (https://t.co/Lb7SUCe2pO) for why this is structurally true. but i think any honest analysis of the economic impacts of AI has to take work creation seriously. 

can jobs be decomposed into tasks?
yes, that is a useful lens. but lists of tasks is a way of looking at jobs—one that makes the question of how much of a job is automatable actually tractable. therefore, it's useful.

but this is not the full picture, it's just jobs as exposed to our method of questioning. 

a good example: under this model, where do the new tasks come from? are they just from bosses that add a list to the task list for workers to complete? where do those tasks come from? unless you can model that well you are missing a key term in the analysis (see the first point above.)

another way of looking at this, borrowing from wittgenstein and heidegger, is that a job is a particular way of seeing and caring about the world. an editor notices things a nurse doesn’t, and vice versa. what you care about shapes what you notice, what seems worth doing, and what counts as doing it well. you can make some of that explicit as a task list. but as your tools and circumstances change, the same cares can generate entirely new tasks. that process is part of the job.

the above is completely missing from this analysis (understandably because it's, by definition, very hard to model!) 

but if you take it seriously, it shoudl substantially change your perspective automation and jobs

Good reminder here that with rapidly accelerating AI progress, you should likely be building with a vision that contemplates at least a few orders of magnitude of capability improvement or token volume available to you.

The best opportunities right now are those where you can value to customers today with things that are barely only possible, but with a full mission that feels nearly impossible with today’s tech.

There are lots of products the require orders of magnitude more processing of data (and thus are barely economically viable ideas) or where model capabilities still are in their infancy relative to what’s needed to work. Best to be building for those scenarios.
tweets.summary_zh: 有个重要提醒，就是在快速发展的 AI 领域，咱们应该设定一个远大的目标，考虑到未来可能会有巨大的能力提升。现在最好的机会是找到那些用今天的技术刚刚能做到的事情，同时大目标几乎是“不可能完成”的。许多产品需要处理大量数据 (处理数据的能力)，而这些技术目前还很初级，所以最好专注于这些前景广阔的挑战。

tweets.text:
The AI jobs prediction so far is playing out the opposite of what many thought.

The reason this is happening is because AI is bringing automation to areas that don’t have finite demand characteristics. AI allows companies to do far more than they could before, but agents still require human operators and oversight to generate value from them. 

And not only has AI not replaced many of the types of jobs that theoretically would have been most affected by AI - engineers or lawyers - but AI is also creating or growing entire categories of jobs across the economy. 

Cybersecurity, FDEs, agent operators, engineers in non-software domains, and tons of job categories are going to explode. It’s not clear if or when this trend will reverse because we keep discovering all new areas of demand that AI is going to open up.
tweets.summary_zh: AI 带来的工作变化和大家预想的正好相反。其实，AI 自动化了很多需求不有限的领域，虽然它能让公司做更多的事情，但仍然需要人来操作和监管这些系统。而且，AI 并没有像有些人担心的那样取代很多工作，比如工程师和律师。反而它正在创造很多新的就业机会，比如网络安全、代理操作员等，很多行业都会因此大幅增长。未来这个趋势还会继续发展。

Pick a workflow you know well - from your personal life or your work.

Automate the whole thing with AI.

tweets.text:
Super bullish on WebMCP. Much like Tesla FSD meets the world where it is (streets, stoplights, potholes and all), agents *need* to ride the existing WWW infrastructure… WebMCP makes it more efficient.

Some pretty unique wins too. e.g: Next.js dev pages could expose debugging tools directly to agents in the specific tab they’re testing, with page-specific context, instead of sifting through server logs. No separate MCP server to find and configure because the page directly exposes its own 'agent tools'.

e.g: in this world 𝚏𝚡 + 𝚊𝚐𝚎𝚗𝚝-𝚋𝚛𝚘𝚠𝚜𝚎𝚛 is a complete web dev stack with zero loss in debugging depth
tweets.summary_zh:
对WebMCP的未来超级看好。就像特斯拉的自动驾驶技术能够适应现实世界（街道、红绿灯、 potholes（坑洼）），AI应用也需要基于现有的网络基础设施。WebMCP让这一切变得更高效。

举个例子，使用Next.js开发的页面可以直接向AI提供调试工具，专注于它们正在测试的特定页面，而不是在服务器日志中翻找。这样就不需要单独找和配置MCP服务器，因为页面会直接提供自己的“代理工具”。

总之，在这种环境下，结合𝚏𝚡和𝚊𝚐𝚎𝚗𝚝-𝚋𝚛𝚘𝚠𝚜𝚎𝚛，就能创建一个完整的网络开发工具组合，同时保证调试的深度不受影响。

tweets.text:
GPT-6 Astra is out. We've been testing the model in early preview on our enterprise complex work eval at Box. It is now the best model we've ever tested on our expanded and hardest test set.

Overall, GPT-6 Astra offers a breakthrough level of capability in coding, analytics, logic, and domain specific knowledge for dealing with complex enterprise knowledge work. In our eval, we use the GPT-6 Astra model in the Box Agent and give it a set of difficult tasks that represent real-world work in various industries. These tasks often will take people hours to execute properly and require deep domain expertise.

GPT-6 Astra scored 77% overall vs. 74% with GPT-5.6 Sol, representing frontier performance. But the story is in some of the bigger gains on individual task types that are incredibly complex across. Here are a few examples across the tests that show how much of an impact this will be in different industries:

* Media and entertainment (48% → 100%, +52 points). Ranking film genres and countries by profitability across a year of production data from four teams, where the trick is to apply the following year's tax-incentive corrections without double-counting them. GPT-6 Astra was perfect on every attempt. Sol had the rankings right but the underlying ratios were wrong.

* Technology (69% → 97%, +28 points). Choosing which region to fund first, from a stack of performance and infrastructure documents that never state the metric the brief asks for. GPT-6 Astra flagged the gap, labelled its own figure a proxy, and caught a growth claim that didn't match the numbers beneath it. GPT-5.6 Sol reported the proxy as the real thing.

* Legal (69% → 93%, +24 points). Reviewing an NDA against a company's own contracting policy, where reaching the right verdict isn't enough; the answer has to cite the provision behind it. Both models declined to approve the draft, but only GPT-6 Astra separated whether the liability cap's structure was permissible from whether its amount was defensible, and pointed to the policy language that settles it. GPT-5.6 Sol argued the same conclusion without citing the provision, which is a critical error in the legal industry.

* Healthcare (53% → 77%, +23 points). Auditing a batch of radiology reports for errors and rating how serious each one is. GPT-6 Astra caught a terminology error in a knee-imaging report that GPT-5.6 Sol missed on both attempts, and was more reliable at grading severity rather than just flagging that something was wrong.

* Energy (82% → 97%, +15 points). Building a consumption report on two facilities from a year of meter logs, where only one of the two sites is actually missing data. GPT-6 Astra found it and drew a line most reviewers wouldn't: the other site's odd solar readings are a measurement problem to investigate, not a gap in the record. GPT-5.6 Sol reported both sites as incomplete.

Astra clearly is going to offer a meaningful jump in powering and orchestrating enterprise workflows. We'll be making GPT-6 Astra as an option in the Box AI Studio for customers to build agents with shortly as it continues to roll out.

tweets.text:
Every AI product should be working towards abstracting model choice away from users. 

In any product, the intelligence is the underlying engine - all the user cares about is that the job gets done. 

Model picking is too much cognitive load for the user.

There have been multiple attempts to abstract model choice away from users. I think we’re finally at the point where this can work well.

It takes three things:

1/ Deep understanding of the model frontier across different weight classes for your particular use cases.

2/ Great evals for your workflows, so you know which models work best where.

3/ A team with the talent and AI-native operating model to continuously adapt as the frontier moves.

Having worked with the Lovable team, I can say they have all three.
tweets.summary_zh: 每个 AI 产品都应该努力简化用户选择模型的过程。用户最关心的是能否完成任务，而不是挑选背后的复杂模型。现在我们终于有了可能实现这一点的条件，包括对模型的深入理解、有效的评估系统和有能力的团队。我认为 Lovable 团队具备了这些条件。

这个视频探讨了生产力的边界如何影响我们的工作方式，并讨论了在追求效率的过程中，有些传统做法反而被重新审视。通过分析当今社会对生产力的期望，节目主持人提出了一些洞察，帮助人们理解如何更好地适应变化。

💡 值得一看 — 此视频涉及生产力与效率的关系，与创意设计和电商运营都有所关联，可以为 Yves 提供思考和灵感。

podcasts.name: Matt Wolfe
podcasts.title: Lex Fridman on programming with AI agents by recording long audio notes
podcasts.summary_zh:
这个视频主要讨论了 Lex Fridman 如何通过录制长音频笔记来与 AI 助手进行编程。这种方法可能会改变我们与 AI 交互的方式，使得创作者能够更轻松地将想法转化为可执行的代码或设计。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 这个视频探讨了使用 AI 助手进行创意编程的方法，与你在 Logic Labs 和 TexTale 的相关工作及创意设计密切相关。

podcasts.name: Matt Wolfe
podcasts.title: Burnout from programming with AI agents | DHH and Lex Fridman
podcasts.summary_zh:
在这期视频中，DHH 和 Lex Fridman 探讨了利用 AI 代理进行编程过程中所带来的倦怠感，讨论了这种技术如何影响程序员的心理健康和工作效率。他们分享了个人经历以及如何在使用 AI 工具时保持创造力和灵活性。

💡 值得一看 — 这个视频结合了 AI 工具的使用体验，对于 Yves 在创意设计和品牌营销中如何有效运用 AI 提供了有价值的见解。

podcasts.name: Matt Wolfe
podcasts.title: Best AI model for coding: Fable vs Opus 5 vs Sol vs Grok vs DeepSeek | DHH and Lex Fridman
podcasts.summary_zh:
这个视频讨论了五种不同的AI编程模型（Fable、Opus 5、Sol、Grok和DeepSeek），由DHH和Lex Fridman分享了它们在编写代码方面的优劣。观看者可以了解到这些模型的功能特点，以及它们在实际应用中的表现和适用场景。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 这些AI编程模型可能对Logic Labs在开发工具和TexTale在电商运营中的应用有所启发，对提升创意设计和产品开发效率尤为重要。

podcasts.name: Matt Wolfe
podcasts.title: Strategies for programming with AI agents | DHH and Lex Fridman
podcasts.summary_zh:
这个视频讨论了使用 AI 智能体进行编程的策略，DHH 和 Lex Fridman 分享了如何通过 AI 来提高编程效率和创造性。视频中探讨了 AI 在开发中的应用，如何借助 AI 工具来优化工作流程，以及潜在的未来发展方向，对开发者和设计师都非常有启发。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 这个视频中提到的 AI 编程策略与 Logic Labs 和 TexTale 的创意设计和电商运营密切相关，有助于提升你的项目效率和创造性。

podcasts.name: Peter Yang
podcasts.title: Why AI shouldn't do the thinking for your kid
podcasts.summary_zh:
视频讨论了为什么不应该让人工智能替代孩子的思考能力。Peter Yang 强调了思维能力的重要性，认为虽然AI可以辅助学习和提供信息，但最终的决策和理解应该由孩子自己完成，以促进他们的批判性思维和创造力的发展。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 这个视频能帮助您更好地理解 AI 在教育中的角色，对创意设计和 TexTale 品牌营销中的“人机协作”思维有启发。

podcasts.name: Matt Wolfe
podcasts.title: Ubuntu vs Omarchy: DHH responds to doubters - Can you build a better Linux distro? | Lex Fridman
podcasts.summary_zh:
视频中，DHH（David Heinemeier Hansson）回应了对Ubuntu和Omarchy两种Linux发行版的质疑，讨论了创建更好的Linux发行版的可行性。他分享了自己在开发中的经验以及对Linux生态系统的看法，强调了创新与用户反馈的重要性。

💡 值得一看 — 了解DHH对开源社区和新技术的见解，可能激发您在创意设计与电商运营上新的思路。

podcasts.name: Data Driven NYC
podcasts.title: Is It Already Too Late to Stop AI? His Honest Answer #ai #podcast
podcasts.summary_zh:
这个视频探讨了当前环境下阻止人工智能快速发展的可能性，并分享了专家对此问题的看法。讨论涉及技术进步的不可逆性，以及在此背景下我们如何应对相关挑战和机遇。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 这个视频涉及AI的未来趋势，对Logic Labs和TexTale在产品开发和品牌战略中应用AI的思考非常有价值。

podcasts.name: No Priors
podcasts.title: AI Agents Are Wiping Databases
podcasts.summary_zh:
这个视频探讨了人工智能代理如何潜在地影响和清理数据库，可能改变传统的数据管理和存储方式。它深入分析了AI代理在数据处理中的作用与挑战，以及在未来企业运营中的应用场景。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 这个话题与 Logic Labs 的 AI 产品开发密切相关，有助于探索AI在数据管理中的应用，提升电商业务和创意设计的效率。

podcasts.name: Matt Wolfe
podcasts.title: Advice for programmers: Learn where state of the art is | DHH and Lex Fridman
podcasts.summary_zh:
这个视频主要是关于程序员在当前技术环境中如何保持竞争力，以及他们应该学习的前沿技术。DHH 和 Lex Fridman 讨论了持续学习的重要性，以及如何利用最新的工具和趋势来提升产品开发和创造力。

💡 值得一看 — 这个视频提供了关于科技行业前沿的见解，可以帮助您更好地理解创意设计和电商中的技术发展趋势。

podcasts.name: Peter Yang
podcasts.title: AI Makes Cheating Easy. Here’s How It Can Make Kids Smarter Instead | Sue Khim
podcasts.summary_zh:
这个视频讨论了人工智能如何让学生在学习过程中变得更加依赖，但同时也探讨了它如何能够提升孩子们的智能水平，而不仅仅是单纯的作弊工具。通过适当的引导和应用，AI可以帮助孩子们更好地理解和掌握知识，而不是简化学习过程。

💡 值得一看 — 视频中关于AI在教育中的潜力的讨论，能够为Yves提供关于AI工具在创意设计与电商运营方面的启示，可能对Logic Labs和TexTale的未来项目有参考价值。

podcasts.name: Lenny's Podcast
podcasts.title: Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya (a16z)
podcasts.summary_zh:
这个视频探讨了为何公司运作越来越趋向于循环模式，嘉宾 Anish Acharya 结合实际案例，分析了这种模式的好处和挑战，以及它对企业创新和决策流程的影响。在快速变化的市场中，循环模式帮助公司更灵活地调整战略，满足客户需求。

💡 值得一看 — 视频中对公司如何在循环模式下进行创新分析，可能为 Yves 在 Logic Labs 和 TexTale 的战略调整和创意设计提供有价值的视角。

podcasts.name: Matt Wolfe
podcasts.title: Tetris on Game Boy is one of the greatest video games of all time | DHH and Lex Fridman
podcasts.summary_zh:
这个视频讨论了经典游戏《俄罗斯方块》在Game Boy上的影响力，特别是它如何成为历史上最伟大的电子游戏之一。主持人DHH和Lex Fridman回忆了该游戏的设计理念，以及它对游戏界的深远影响。

💡 值得一看 — 该视频探讨了经典设计如何在科技与创意交汇的背景下产生影响，对理解创意设计工具在当今行业中的位置及应用有启发性。

podcasts.name: The AI Daily Brief
podcasts.title: How to Build an AI-Native Company Today
podcasts.summary_zh:
这个视频探讨了如何在当今快速发展的科技环境中建立一家以人工智能为核心的公司，分享了成功案例和实用策略。通过分析市场需求和技术趋势，视频强调了整合AI技术的重要性，并提供了从零开始发展的实用步骤。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 该内容直接涉及创业和AI工具的应用，能为Logic Labs和TexTale的创意设计提供有价值的洞察。

podcasts.name: Matt Wolfe
podcasts.title: Why DHH doesn't miss programming without AI | Lex Fridman Podcast Clips
podcasts.summary_zh:
在这期视频中，主持人Lex Fridman与DHH（Ruby on Rails的创始人）讨论了他在没有AI的情况下对编程的看法。DHH分享了自己如何看待AI对软件开发的影响，以及他对未来科技趋势的独到见解，强调了AI在编程中的潜力。

💡 值得一看 — DHH的观点可以为Yves在Logic Labs和TexTale的创意设计中提供新的思考方向，尤其是在如何利用AI提升产品开发和品牌营销的效率。

podcasts.name: Matt Wolfe
podcasts.title: Rust is the ugliest programming language invented in the last 40 years | DHH and Lex Fridman
podcasts.summary_zh:
在这个视频中，DHH 和 Lex Fridman 讨论了 Rust 编程语言为何被认为是过去四十年中最丑陋的编程语言之一。他们探讨了 Rust 的设计哲学、开发者的体验以及在现代软件开发中的适用性，带着一定的幽默感揭示了编程语言背后的争议。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 由于你在 Logic Labs 和 TexTale 的工作，了解 Rust 语言的优劣势或许能为未来的 AI 工具和电商平台开发提供一些启示，尤其是在创造性设计和技术实现的交汇点上。

podcasts.name: Matt Wolfe
podcasts.title: Is programming dead? | DHH and Lex Fridman
podcasts.summary_zh:
这个视频讨论了编程在现代科技和商业环境中的地位，特别是由 DHH（Basecamp 的联合创始人）和 Lex Fridman 的对话引导，提出了编程是否仍然是未来的必要技能的问题。两位嘉宾探讨了无代码工具的崛起以及这些工具如何改变开发和创作方式，特别是对于非技术人员来说的影响。

🎯 推荐 Yves 观看 — 该视频对零代码工具的讨论与 Logic Labs 和 TexTale 的创意设计和运营策略密切相关，能够为您提供关于如何利用这些工具推动业务发展的新思路。

producthunt.name: Clipto MCP
producthunt.tagline: Let agents source clips from terabytes of your local video
producthunt.summary_zh: Clipto MCP 是一款视频剪辑工具，允许用户从本地海量视频中快速提取片段。它支持高效整理和查找视频素材，方便用户在创作中使用。

producthunt.name: Astute
producthunt.tagline: Automate your B2B brand going viral, with new media creators
producthunt.summary_zh: Astute 是一个自动化平台，帮助企业与新媒体创作者合作，快速提升品牌知名度。通过简化品牌宣传流程，企业可以轻松实现内容的病毒式传播。

producthunt.name: Dograh
producthunt.summary_zh: Dograh 是一个开源的 VAPI 替代方案，旨在提供灵活的 API 解决方案。用户可以使用它创建、管理和测试 API，简化开发过程，提高效率。这个工具支持多种编程语言，方便开发者集成。

producthunt.name: Grok Bot
producthunt.tagline: AI teammates that you can give real work to
producthunt.summary_zh: Grok Bot是一款智能助手，可以作为你的工作搭档执行实际任务。它可以处理信息、回答问题和完成日常工作，让你更高效地完成目标。通过与Grok Bot协作，你可以节省时间和精力。

producthunt.name: Meridian
producthunt.tagline: Don't let your work go unnoticed. Get promoted!
producthunt.summary_zh: Meridian是一款专注于职业发展的工具。它可以帮助用户记录并展示自己的工作成就，让你在职场上获得更多关注和晋升机会。通过使用Meridian，你可以轻松整理和分享自己的工作亮点。

producthunt.name: x1
producthunt.tagline: Lovable for iPhone apps go from idea to App Store
producthunt.summary_zh: x1 是一个帮助用户将想法转化为 iPhone 应用的工具。它提供从概念设计到提交 App Store 的完整流程，用户可以轻松创建和发布自己的应用程序。

producthunt.name: Kilo Code for JetBrains
producthunt.tagline: Fully native, open-source coding agent built for JetBrains
producthunt.summary_zh: Kilo Code for JetBrains 是一款完全原生的开源编码助手，专为 JetBrains 开发环境设计。它能够提高编码效率，提供智能代码建议和自动完成功能，让开发者更轻松地编写程序。

producthunt.name: Switch
producthunt.tagline: Bring any AI agent into Slack, Teams & Discord
producthunt.summary_zh: Switch是一款可以将各种AI助手集成到Slack、Teams和Discord中的工具。用户可以通过这个平台轻松接入不同的AI代理，以提高团队的沟通和协作效率。它简化了工作流程，让员工能够快速获取所需的信息和支持。

producthunt.name: Monid
producthunt.summary_zh: Monid是一个为代理工具提供支持的开放式路由平台。它可以帮助用户快速集成和管理不同的代理工具，提升工作效率。用户可以通过Monid轻松连接和使用各种应用程序。

producthunt.name: GPT-6 Astra
producthunt.tagline: OpenAI's most capable model for end-to-end work
producthunt.summary_zh: GPT-6 Astra 是 OpenAI 最新的人工智能模型，具备强大的自然语言处理能力。它可以完成从文本生成到对话理解等多种任务，适用于自动化工作和内容创作。

producthunt.name: PaymentKit
producthunt.tagline: Billing that survives a processor shutdown
producthunt.summary_zh: PaymentKit是一款支付处理工具，能够在支付处理器出现故障时继续进行账单和交易。它确保用户的付款流程不会中断，提高了支付的可靠性和效率。

producthunt.name: Mastra Factory
producthunt.tagline: From issue to production, run by agents.
producthunt.summary_zh: Mastra Factory 是一个自动化平台，专为管理生产流程而设计。用户可以通过平台提交问题，从而直接将其转化为生产任务，整个过程由代理人进行协调与执行。简而言之，它简化了产品从问题到生产的转化流程。

producthunt.name: Clara AI SDR
producthunt.tagline: Turn website visitors into qualified pipeline
producthunt.summary_zh: Clara AI SDR 是一款自动化的软件工具，可以将访问网站的访客转化为潜在客户。通过智能分析和交互，它能够识别有意向的访客并收集相关信息，帮助企业建立更高效的客户销售漏斗。

producthunt.name: Kane CLI
producthunt.tagline: Natural language browser & mobile app tests from terminal
producthunt.summary_zh: Kane CLI 是一款命令行工具，可以通过自然语言指令执行浏览器和手机应用程序的测试。用户只需输入简单的语言描述，工具便能自动生成相应的测试脚本，提升测试效率。

producthunt.name: Ito
producthunt.tagline: AI code review that runs your code
producthunt.summary_zh: Ito是一款人工智能代码审查工具，可以自动运行你的代码并进行检测。它能找到代码中的错误和优化建议，帮助开发者提升代码质量和效率。

github_trending.description: A skill to stop your coding agent from burying the answer. ADHD-friendly output.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目旨在创建一个能够以简洁明了的方式输出信息的工具，帮助用户更容易获取他们需要的答案，尤其适合ADHD（注意力缺陷多动障碍）患者。对于Yves来说，这个项目可以在Logic Labs（AI 公司）中作为一个创意设计工具，提升团队在开发AI产品时的沟通效率和信息提取能力。在TexTale（科技服装电商）方面，融合这种工具也有助于理解用户反馈和优化客户体验。

github_trending.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

github_trending.description: Open-source 3D architectural editor with a local CLI, MCP tools, and practical workflows for humans and AI agents.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个用于创建和分享3D建筑项目的工具，可以帮助用户轻松地设计和展示建筑作品。对Yves来说，尤其在TexTale的业务中，这个工具可以用来设计和展示男士科技服装的展示场景，提高品牌形象和购物体验。同时，在创意设计方面，它能够激发Yves的创意灵感，让他更好地运用AI技术进行产品创作。

github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目提供了一套用于计算机辅助设计（CAD）、计算机辅助工程（CAE）和计算机辅助制造（CAM）的智能技能库，帮助用户更高效地进行设计和制作。对于Yves来说，这项技术可以在Logic Labs中提升AI在设计过程中的应用，或在TexTale中优化科技服装的设计和生产流程，同时也能激发他作为创意设计从业者的灵感。

github_trending.description: 38 editorial diagram types for Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. Self-contained HTML + SVG. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目提供了38种编辑图表类型，方便用户在网页中创建展示数据或概念的图形，使用HTML和SVG技术，操作简单明了。对Yves而言，这个项目在Logic Labs中可以帮助他更好地展示AI相关的概念和结果，同时也能增强TexTale的产品展示，让男士科技服装的创意设计更具视觉吸引力。

github_trending.description: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个多智能体的金融交易框架，利用大型语言模型（LLM）来帮助进行自动化的股票和金融交易。对于Yves而言，这个项目可以帮助Logic Labs探索金融领域的AI应用，提升其在AI技术上的创意和实用性，同时也能激发他在TexTale电商领域的创新思路，探索将AI技术应用于电商分析和营销策略。
